title: Scheme charts over a pulled-back etale covering
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be an index type and $V_i$ objects of the small etale site of $Y$. Suppose they cover the final sheaf: on every object $T$ of $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, the sieve of arrows $W\to T$ for which there exists a map $W\to V_i$ is covering [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For each $i$ let $\mathcal A(f,V_i)$ be the commuting scheme-chart category of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]: its objects are etale scheme charts $U\to X$ with a scheme map $U\to V_i$ commuting over $Y$. Then the family of all these $U$, indexed by pairs $(i,q)$ with $q\in\mathcal A(f,V_i)$, covers the final sheaf of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ in the same sieve sense. Neither representability of $f$ nor finiteness of $I$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03DO (lemma-local-pullback), proof: the base-changed covering; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03G2 (lemma-functoriality-etale-site).

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas A to Y. On A, the hypothesis gives a covering sieve of scheme charts admitting maps to the V_i. These charts compose with A to cover the final object of the enlarged etale site of Y. Indeed, after pulling back the atlas to any enlarged object, refine by scheme atlases and use the covering sieve on their scheme objects. The scheme-object comparison has exactly these coverings.

The enlarged base-change functor preserves coverings. Pull back this covering to X, and take surjective etale scheme atlases of its algebraic-space members. Each resulting scheme U is etale over X and maps to some V_i over Y, so it defines a commuting chart q in A(f,V_i).

For any scheme chart T of X pull back the preceding cover and refine by scheme atlases. Composition of etale covers gives a covering of T whose arrows lie in the sieve of objects q.left. Upward closure of covering sieves gives the required covering on T. This is precisely CoversTop; if the original indexing family is empty the same covering argument applies.
